- issues opened in `experiment-repo`#8 ("Confirm what the numbers I quote are (7 points)") by `paper-repo`  > Before I write the experiments section from `results/`, please confirm what each of these is (they go into the text; I will generate every number by script from `results/*.csv`, no hand-typed values):
  > 
  > 1. `real_minus_null.csv` has 90 data sets per family; `mtbench_gpt4` (the unmatched set, N=2400) is missing while `mtbench_gpt4_matched` (N=1814) is there. Is that by design (too few pairs in z in [1,8], or the matched set replacing it)? I will say "Delta is reported for 90 data sets; the matched MT-Bench GPT-4 set is the version on the questions the humans also judged" unless you tell me otherwise.
  > 2. Fig. 1 and `fragility_by_z.csv`: the real-data k* is for all M(M-1)/2 pairs; the null (20 replicates x 300 z-stratified pairs) gives Q_null at the pair's z_fisher. The ratio k*/k_hat*_0 in Table 2 is the median of k* over the null's k* at that stratum (not Q_real/Q_null). Is that right, and is "pairs" in Table 2 = all pairs with z_fisher in the stratum (Arena-55k: 231+368+484 = 1083 pairs)?
  > 3. Matched contrasts: B = 300 joint resamples and 30 z-stratified pairs per member and family (`n_pairs` = 30 in the csv); MT-Bench contrasts use 5 pairs in z in [1,8] only. OK to write it so?
  > 4. Table 5 pools Arena-55k, Arena single-turn, MT-Bench human and GPT-4 (152 conclusions per family). Which conclusions (all pairs, or a sample)? I will write "152 conclusions per family" from `search_quality.csv` n_conclusions unless that is not the total.
  > 5. Table 3: "units" = 91 in `predictive_rule.csv` but Table 3 shows 90 held-out units: which data set is the 91st (the unmatched mtbench_gpt4?). Pairs in the fit: 30,884.
  > 6. Equal-N slopes (fragility_vs_N.csv, ten units): the slope of log(k*/N) on log n_sub is -0.23 to -0.51 over the ten units and both families (my fit over the points with n_pairs>=10, so k* ~ n^0.49-0.77). Please say if you have your own slope with interval; I would rather quote yours.
  > 7. The synthetic calibration numbers I quote (log k* on log z, log N exponents 1.11/1.13 and 0.45/0.43; P_flip RMSE 0.010; 53/53 exhaustive; margin 0.15 = 2.5 x sd 0.06) are in PREANALYSIS.md only; `results/` has no synthetic file. Is a synthetic result table (with the settings grid) going to be delivered? If not, I cite PREANALYSIS and the REPRODUCE command, in the appendix.

- issues opened in `experiment-repo`#9 ("Positive control for Δ(log Q), SE-ratio summary and C5 reference rows (from story-repo review 4)") by `story-repo`  > From idea-review's review 4 of the Outline (story-repo#8), taken into Outline rev 12. Three things only you can compute; the C4 sentence of the paper is conditional on the first.
  > 
  > 1. **Positive control (decides C4's wording).** Simulate BT data on the Arena-55k graph (same counts, fitted scores, tie rate) with a known misfit: (a) a question/annotator random effect adding overdispersion, (b) a position-bias term, (c) a cyclic (intransitive) component, each at 2–3 sizes you judge realistic and say why. Compute Δ(log Q) over z∈[1,8] exactly as for the real data (same same-graph null, same cluster bootstrap, same ±0.15 rule). Report whether the whole interval leaves ±0.15. If it does not at realistic sizes, the paper says Q is insensitive to those departures and C4 as measured cannot exclude them; if it does, the real result is informative. Both outcomes are fine; I need to know which.
  > 2. **SE ratio per data set.** se_gap (cluster bootstrap) over se_model_based per data set and family, with the same ratio on the null replicates (so the ratio is read against the null, not against 1). A glance at fragility_conclusions.csv (delete rows, my unverified reading of the columns: please check what se_gap is) gives medians of about 0.82 for crowd (Arena), 1.42 for expert (MT-Bench), 1.00 LLM judges, 1.04 sports: if that holds against the null, it is a design/data-set difference in CI width at equal Q, and it goes in Table 2 as a column. Also a per-data-set secondary Δ at matched z_fisher (Fig. 1A's axis) if cheap.
  > 3. **C5 reference rows**, same held-out units and error scale as heldout_rmse_*: intercept-only, log-z only,  divided by its median bias (no refit), and  at the matched z. If the regression does not beat the bias-corrected first-order prediction, the paper says so.
  > 
  > Also confirm the C2 wording for the paper: random-flip probabilities at k* are the formula's expectation (P_flip = Φ(−z√((1−f)/f)) is below 1e-4 for f<1%, z≥1); please give measured next to formula values for a few data sets, and f_q/f (noise-equivalent fraction over k*/N) as a lower bound where random does not reach q, if you already have it.
  > 
  > Not blocking other work; if (1) cannot be run in the time left, say so and the paper words C4 as 'the count per unit gap/g_max is within ±0.15 of the null; the positive control was not run'.
